name: Weave
rationale: Captures the act of binding independent tasks into a coherent whole. Evokes the diverge-converge pattern: separate threads come together into durable fabric. Strong craft metaphor.
why_creative: Concrete verb with both literal and technical readings. Feels skilled and intentional, not automated chaos.
risk: May feel too artisanal for infrastructure tooling

name: Attest
rationale: Verification is the core primitive. Every task must attest to its correctness via shell checks. Formal, trustworthy, and distinct from generic AI agent language.
why_creative: Legal/formal term that maps perfectly to check-based execution. Uncommon in dev tools.
risk: May feel too formal or enterprise-heavy

name: Bind
rationale: Short, strong verb for connecting independent pieces into a verified whole. Evokes both the DAG structure and the contract between tasks.
why_creative: One syllable, crisp consonants, works as CLI command. Technical and craft readings.
risk: DNS software already uses this name

name: Seam
rationale: Where pieces join. The DAG edges, the task boundaries, the verification points. A seam is both connection and inspection point.
why_creative: Concrete noun with structural meaning. Implies careful joining, not random assembly.
risk: May be too subtle or require explanation

name: Trace
rationale: The execution path through the DAG. The evidence left behind. The ability to see exactly what ran and what passed.
why_creative: Technical primitive with observability connotations. Clean, simple, ownable.
risk: Observability tools may have claimed this space

name: Ledger
rationale: Immutable record of what ran, what passed, what was cached. Evokes trust, accountability, and deterministic execution.
why_creative: Financial/accounting metaphor that maps to verifiable execution history. Serious and trustworthy.
risk: Blockchain associations may confuse positioning

name: Stitch
rationale: Binding tasks together with precision. Each stitch is a verified connection. The final artifact is stronger than its parts.
why_creative: Craft metaphor with technical precision. Implies care and skill, not automation.
risk: May feel too craft-focused for infrastructure

name: Seal
rationale: Verification creates a seal of approval. Tasks are sealed when checks pass. Short, strong, and evokes trust.
why_creative: One syllable, multiple meanings (seal of approval, cryptographic seal, watertight seal). All map to verification.
risk: May be too generic or have existing tool conflicts

name: Knot
rationale: Where threads converge. A knot is both a joining point and a structural element. Short, memorable, and evokes the DAG structure.
why_creative: Concrete noun with graph-theory resonance (knot theory). Extremely short and ownable.
risk: Spelling/pronunciation confusion (silent K)

name: Cord
rationale: Multiple strands twisted together for strength. Evokes the parallel execution and convergence pattern.
why_creative: Four letters, one syllable, strong metaphor for combining independent pieces.
risk: May feel too simple or lack technical weight

name: Tether
rationale: Tasks are tethered to their checks. The playbook tethers chaos to determinism. Evokes control and reliability.
why_creative: Implies controlled freedom — agents can diverge but remain tethered to verification.
risk: May imply constraint rather than empowerment

name: Lace
rationale: Intricate binding pattern. Tasks lace together into a verified structure. Short, visual, and evokes precision.
why_creative: Four letters, one syllable, strong visual metaphor for DAG structure.
risk: May feel too delicate for infrastructure

name: Weft
rationale: The horizontal threads in weaving that bind the vertical warp into fabric. Metaphor for how Converge weaves independent agent tasks into a verified whole.
why_creative: Four letters, concrete craft term, implies structure and binding without saying orchestration. Strong CLI feel.
risk: May be unfamiliar to non-craft audiences, but pronunciation is clear.

name: Cadence
rationale: Musical term for rhythmic flow and resolution. Maps to Converge's loop-until-checks-pass rhythm and the feeling of work reaching completion.
why_creative: Premium developer brand (Cadence Design Systems), implies reliable rhythm and resolution, not chaotic flow.
risk: Existing enterprise software brand, though in different domain (EDA tools).

name: Anvil
rationale: The foundational tool where metal is shaped through repeated strikes. Metaphor for the runtime that hammers tasks until checks pass.
why_creative: Concrete, durable, implies strength and precision. Strong single-syllable feel for CLI.
risk: Could feel heavy or industrial rather than modern/fast.

name: Bearing
rationale: Navigation term for precise direction. Converge gives teams a bearing through complex AI work with DAG-based execution.
why_creative: Technical precision metaphor, implies direction and confidence, avoids flow/agent clichés.
risk: Multiple meanings (direction, mechanical part, endurance) could dilute focus.

name: Lattice
rationale: Mathematical structure of interconnected nodes. Converge compiles playbooks into a lattice of verified tasks.
why_creative: Graph metaphor without saying graph, implies elegant structure and mathematical rigor.
risk: Existing semiconductor company (Lattice Semi), may feel slightly abstract.

name: Keystone
rationale: The central stone in an arch that locks all other pieces in place. Converge is the keystone that makes AI agent work reliable.
why_creative: Architectural metaphor for structural integrity and the piece that makes everything hold.
risk: Longer (8 letters), existing pipeline product (Keystone in OpenStack).

name: Tally
rationale: A verified count or record. Converge tallies task completion through shell-command checks, not vibes.
why_creative: Short, concrete, implies accountability and verified counting. Strong CLI command feel.
risk: Could feel accounting-focused rather than developer-tool focused.

name: Span
rationale: The distance or structure that bridges two points. Converge spans from chaotic prompts to verified outputs.
why_creative: Four letters, architectural and graph-theory meanings, implies bridging and coverage.
risk: Very short and broad, may be hard to own in search/trademark.

name: Temper
rationale: The process of heating and cooling metal to achieve precise strength. Converge tempers AI output through iterative checks.
why_creative: Craft metaphor for refinement through process, implies precision and durability.
risk: Multiple meanings (mood, metal process) could create confusion.

name: Rhumb
rationale: A navigation line of constant bearing. Converge provides a constant bearing through AI work with playbook-based execution.
why_creative: Rare, ownable, technical navigation term. Five letters, distinctive sound.
risk: Unfamiliar word, pronunciation not obvious from spelling.

name: Quire
rationale: A set of folded sheets forming part of a book. Converge assembles independent task outputs into a complete, bound artifact.
why_creative: Publishing metaphor for assembled verified work, distinctive and ownable.
risk: Archaic term, may feel too literary for developer tools.

name: Dovetail
rationale: A precise woodworking joint where pieces interlock perfectly. Converge dovetails agent tasks into verified execution.
why_creative: Craft metaphor for precision fit and interlocking parts, implies quality and care.
risk: Longer (8 letters), verb form means 'to fit together' which is positive but may feel descriptive.

name: Spline
rationale: A flexible strip used in drafting to draw smooth curves, or a ridge that fits into a groove. Converge splines together agent tasks.
why_creative: Technical term with both craft and mathematical meanings, implies smooth connection.
risk: May feel too technical/CAD-specific, existing graphics term.

name: Folio
rationale: A sheet of paper folded once, or a collection of works. Converge produces a folio of verified task outputs.
why_creative: Publishing metaphor for collected verified work, implies portfolio and completeness.
risk: May feel too publishing-specific, existing design/portfolio connotations.

name: Verus
rationale: Latin for 'true' or 'genuine.' Maps directly to the product's core promise: checks verify truth, not vibes. A DAG-based build system that proves correctness through shell commands.
why_creative: Single Latin root that feels modern and technical. Owns the verification space without saying 'check' or 'test.' Works as a CLI command and carries weight.
risk: May feel academic to some; needs strong visual identity to feel modern.

name: Telos
rationale: Greek for 'end' or 'purpose.' Every task in Converge has a telos: the checks that define done. The runtime loops until it reaches that end state.
why_creative: Philosophical depth without pretension. Two syllables, clean sound, owns the 'done state' concept. Feels calm and purposeful.
risk: Pronunciation ambiguity (English vs Greek). May feel too philosophical for some developers.

name: Praxis
rationale: Greek for 'practice' or 'action.' Converge turns theory (prompts) into repeatable practice (playbooks). Execution over conversation.
why_creative: Developer-familiar from 'best practices.' Short, crisp, action-oriented. Feels like a tool for practitioners.
risk: Already used in some dev contexts (GraphQL Praxis). May feel too academic.

name: Opus
rationale: Latin for 'work' or 'masterpiece.' A playbook is an opus: structured, repeatable, version-controlled work. The output of a DAG run is an opus.
why_creative: Familiar word with gravitas. Implies quality and craft. Short, memorable, works as a CLI command. Musical and technical connotations.
risk: May feel too artistic or classical. Anthropic's Claude Opus model creates association.

name: Iter
rationale: Latin for 'journey' or 'path.' A playbook is an iter through a DAG. The runtime follows the path until checks converge.
why_creative: Short, technical, implies motion without saying 'flow.' Developer-familiar from 'iterate.' Clean CLI command.
risk: Pronunciation ambiguity. May feel too generic (iteration is everywhere in dev).

name: Ergon
rationale: Greek for 'work' or 'task.' The fundamental unit in Converge is a task. Ergon is the work that gets done, verified by checks.
why_creative: Technical root (ergonomics, energy) with a strong sound. Two syllables, hard consonants. Feels like a build tool.
risk: Less familiar than other Greek roots. May need explanation.

name: Taxon
rationale: Greek root 'taxis' (arrangement, order) + '-on' suffix. Converge arranges tasks into a DAG, orders execution topologically, and organizes chaos into structure.
why_creative: Biology-familiar (taxonomy) but fresh in dev tools. Implies classification and order. Short, crisp, memorable.
risk: May feel too scientific. Taxonomy association could be limiting.

name: Verax
rationale: Latin 'verax' means 'truthful' or 'accurate.' A coined form blending 'verus' (true) with a modern '-ax' ending. Checks verify truth; the runtime is truthful about what passed.
why_creative: Feels modern and technical while rooted in Latin. Hard 'x' ending gives it edge. Owns verification without being literal.
risk: Coined form may feel invented. Less immediately recognizable than 'verus.'

name: Syntex
rationale: Greek 'syn' (together) + 'tex' (weave/build). Converge weaves independent tasks together into a coherent DAG. Parallel execution, unified result.
why_creative: Modern coined name with clear roots. Implies synthesis and construction. Short, memorable, works as a CLI command.
risk: '-tex' suffix may feel generic (Latex, Cortex). Coined form needs strong execution.

name: Nexum
rationale: Latin 'nexum' means 'bond' or 'connection.' Converge binds tasks into a DAG, connects checks to outputs, and links playbooks to execution.
why_creative: Familiar root (nexus) with a fresh ending. Implies connection without being literal. Short, strong, memorable.
risk: Close to 'Nexus' which is widely used. May feel derivative.

name: Telon
rationale: Greek 'telos' (end, purpose) with a modern '-on' suffix. Every task has a telon: the checks that define completion. The runtime seeks the telon.
why_creative: Coined form that feels technical and modern. Particle physics vibe ('-on' like electron, photon). Owns the 'done state' concept.
risk: Coined form may need explanation. Less immediately meaningful than 'telos.'

name: Graphon
rationale: Greek 'graph' (write, draw) + '-on' suffix. Converge writes execution graphs, draws DAGs, and records evidence. A playbook is a graphon.
why_creative: Technical root with a modern suffix. Implies structure and recording. Short, memorable, works as a CLI command.
risk: Too close to 'graph' which is crowded in dev tools. May feel too literal.

name: Iterum
rationale: Latin 'iterum' means 'again' or 'repeatedly.' Converge loops until checks pass. Playbooks are repeatable. Same inputs, same outputs.
why_creative: Latin root that feels technical and precise. Implies repeatability without saying 'loop.' Three syllables but flows well.
risk: Three syllables may be too long. Less familiar than 'iter.'

name: Praxon
rationale: Greek 'praxis' (action, practice) + '-on' suffix. A coined form that feels like a technical primitive. Converge turns prompts into praxons: executable, verifiable actions.
why_creative: Coined form with strong roots. Particle physics vibe. Implies action and execution. Short, memorable, technical.
risk: Coined form may feel invented. Close to 'Praxis' which is already used.

name: Verum
rationale: Latin 'verum' means 'truth' or 'reality.' Converge verifies truth through shell commands. The runtime seeks verum: the state where all checks pass.
why_creative: Latin root that feels modern and technical. Owns verification without being literal. Short, strong, memorable.
risk: May feel academic. Close to 'Verus' which is also in this list.

name: Rivet
rationale: A rivet permanently binds metal pieces through a mechanical process—matching how Converge binds independent agent tasks into a verified whole. Strong craft metaphor with precision and permanence.
why_creative: Concrete craft term that evokes durable joining without workflow clichés. One syllable feel, excellent CLI command.
risk: May feel industrial/hardware-focused without context.

name: Tack
rationale: Nautical term for changing course by adjusting sails; also a fastener. Captures both navigation and binding—core to DAG execution and task coordination.
why_creative: Four letters, one syllable, dual metaphor (navigation + fastening). Perfect shell command brevity.
risk: May be too terse or ambiguous without brand context.

name: Proof
rationale: Direct reference to verification artifacts and the core promise: shell-command checks, not vibes. Also evokes publishing proofs and mathematical proof.
why_creative: Five letters, one syllable, triple metaphor (verification, publishing, math). Matches product truth perfectly.
risk: May feel too literal or narrow to QA/testing category.

name: Gauge
rationale: Precision measurement tool that ensures fit and tolerance. Matches the check-based verification loop and the feeling of knowing exactly what passed.
why_creative: Five letters, craft precision metaphor, implies measurement without saying monitoring. Strong developer fit.
risk: Spelling may require clarification (gauge vs gage).

name: Helm
rationale: Navigation control point—where you steer the ship. Evokes calm control and directed execution without workflow engine clichés.
why_creative: Four letters, one syllable, navigation metaphor with control and direction. Excellent CLI feel.
risk: Kubernetes package manager already uses this name.

name: Sigil
rationale: A seal or signature mark that proves authenticity—connects to verification artifacts and the fingerprint caching that ensures reproducibility.
why_creative: Five letters, unusual but pronounceable, evokes seals and proof without being literal. Ownable.
risk: May feel mystical or unfamiliar; pronunciation not immediately obvious.

name: Plumb
rationale: Tool for finding true vertical—craft metaphor for correctness and alignment. Matches the check-based loop that ensures work is true.
why_creative: Five letters, one syllable, craft precision metaphor. Strong verb and noun forms.
risk: May feel too niche or construction-focused.

name: Quay
rationale: Structured dock where ships load and unload—evokes the coordination point where independent work converges into a stable artifact.
why_creative: Four letters, one syllable, unusual spelling creates ownability. Navigation metaphor without saying flow.
risk: Spelling/pronunciation mismatch may cause friction.

name: Latch
rationale: Fastening mechanism that clicks into place—evokes the moment when checks pass and work locks into done state. Simple and mechanical.
why_creative: Five letters, one syllable, concrete mechanism for completion and holding state. Good CLI command.
risk: May feel too small or mechanical without broader context.

name: Berth
rationale: Designated space where a ship docks—evokes the stable position where work comes to rest after navigation. Calm control and completion.
why_creative: Five letters, one syllable, navigation metaphor for stable completion. Uncommon in dev tools.
risk: May feel too nautical or niche; pronunciation could be unclear.

name: Canon
rationale: Musical form where independent voices follow the same rule—perfect metaphor for DAG execution where tasks follow playbook contracts independently.
why_creative: Five letters, musical metaphor for coordinated independent execution. Premium sound, multiple meanings (rule, standard).
risk: Camera brand association; may feel too formal or religious.

name: Waypoint
rationale: Navigation checkpoint metaphor. Each task is a verified waypoint in a larger journey. Matches task-by-task convergence model.
why_creative: Clear progress metaphor without flow/pipeline language. Developer-friendly compound word.
risk: Longer (8 letters); may feel slightly generic in DevOps context.

name: Rite
rationale: Ritual/completion metaphor. Each task is a rite that must be completed before moving forward. Implies ceremony and trustworthy progression.
why_creative: Four letters, unexpected semantic territory. Avoids all AI/workflow clichés.
risk: Homophone with 'right' and 'write'; may cause confusion in speech.

name: Joinery
rationale: Craft precision metaphor. The art of fitting pieces together with exact tolerances. Matches DAG assembly and multi-agent coordination.
why_creative: Woodworking craft term that implies skill and precision. Distinctive territory.
risk: Three syllables, slightly longer; may feel artisanal rather than technical.

name: Mesh
rationale: Graph theory without saying graph. Distributed network where nodes coordinate. Matches multi-agent DAG execution model.
why_creative: Four letters, one syllable, technical networking term. Strong CLI feel.
risk: Service mesh is a crowded infrastructure category; may blend in.

name: Signoff
rationale: Ritual/completion metaphor. Each task requires signoff before the next begins. Matches check-based gates and verification model.
why_creative: Clear completion metaphor, developer-native term (code review signoff).
risk: Two words compressed; may feel corporate or approval-heavy.

name: Vex
rationale: Three-letter monosyllable with sharp consonant energy. Evokes precision and technical rigor. Works perfectly as a CLI command and has the brevity of Bun or Fly.
why_creative: Extremely short and memorable, with a technical edge that avoids generic AI/workflow language. The hard 'x' ending gives it command-line authority.
risk: Could be perceived as negative (to vex = to annoy), though brevity and product context may override this.

name: Flux
rationale: Classic technical term for flow and change. Strong consonant frame (fl-x) with motion and transformation associations. Already familiar in developer contexts (Redux Flux pattern).
why_creative: Balances familiarity with technical credibility. The 'x' ending gives it CLI snap, and the motion metaphor aligns with DAG execution.
risk: Somewhat crowded in developer tooling (Flux architecture, Influx, etc.). May feel less ownable.

name: Knit
rationale: Four-letter monosyllable from weaving/binding metaphor. Implies careful coordination and durable construction. Warm craft associations with technical precision.
why_creative: Craft metaphor that makes coordination feel intentional and skilled, like Playwright. Avoids AI/workflow clichés entirely.
risk: Silent 'k' creates spelling ambiguity. Craft metaphor may feel too soft for enterprise positioning.

name: Anchor
rationale: Six-letter two-syllable word with stability and foundation metaphor. Implies reliable grounding and trustworthy execution.
why_creative: Strong stability and trust associations. Familiar word that gains depth from product context, like Stripe or Linear.
risk: Common metaphor in tech (anchor links, anchor tags). May feel generic without strong differentiation.

name: Locus
rationale: Five-letter two-syllable word with mathematical and spatial precision. Implies central point and convergence. Clean Latin root.
why_creative: Mathematical term that evokes convergence and fixed points. Premium sound with technical depth. Avoids crowded zones.
risk: May feel abstract or academic. Latin root could seem generic SaaS without strong product connection.

name: Nexus
rationale: Five-letter two-syllable word implying connection and central coordination. Strong consonant frame (n-x-s) with technical authority.
why_creative: Familiar technical term that evokes connection and coordination without AI/workflow clichés. Strong phonetic presence.
risk: Heavily used in tech (Google Nexus, Sonatype Nexus). May lack distinctiveness and domain availability.

name: Warp
rationale: Four-letter monosyllable from weaving territory. Implies structure, speed, and transformation. Strong technical and sci-fi associations.
why_creative: Weaving metaphor (warp and weft) with speed associations (warp speed). Distinctive and memorable with strong CLI feel.
risk: Sci-fi associations may feel playful rather than enterprise-serious. Existing tools (Warp terminal) create collision risk.

name: Galley
rationale: Publishing term for proof sheets before final printing. Perfect metaphor for reviewable, verifiable agent output before production. Editorial precision meets developer workflow.
why_creative: Brings publishing's proof-reading rigor to AI execution. Implies inspectable artifacts and careful review—not black-box automation.
risk: May evoke ships or kitchens before publishing context is established.

name: Bound
rationale: Mathematical term for limits and constraints. Also: tied together, headed toward a destination. Captures both convergence and the binding of tasks into a whole.
why_creative: Dual meaning (mathematical bounds, bound together) with clean phonetics. Implies both precision and coordination.
risk: Common word; may need strong brand to own in dev-tool space.

name: Rhizome
rationale: Botanical term for underground stem networks that spread and connect. Maps to distributed agent execution and DAG topology. Unexpected and memorable.
why_creative: Brings organic network intelligence to technical execution. Feels sophisticated and distinctive—not generic AI tooling.
risk: Unfamiliar term; may need explanation. Pronunciation not immediately obvious.

name: Invariant
rationale: Mathematical property that remains unchanged through transformations. Core to the product promise: same inputs, same outputs, deterministic execution.
why_creative: Precise technical term that captures the product's determinism promise. Feels serious and trustworthy.
risk: Longer (9 letters, 3 syllables); may feel academic or enterprise-heavy.

name: Tempo
rationale: Musical timing and pace. Aligns with execution rhythm and controlled progress. Five letters, bright vowels, excellent command feel.
why_creative: Musical metaphor that implies speed and control without saying 'fast'. Memorable and command-friendly.
risk: May feel too casual or music-specific without product context.

name: Clasp
rationale: Binding and secure connection. Aligns with DAG assembly and task coordination. Five letters, strong consonants.
why_creative: Physical binding metaphor that feels precise and trustworthy. Uncommon in dev-tool naming.
risk: May feel too physical or jewelry-like without product context.

name: Ariadne
rationale: Ariadne gave Theseus the thread to navigate the labyrinth and return safely. Perfect metaphor for a system that guides agents through complex DAGs and ensures they converge back with proof.
why_creative: Strong narrative archetype of thread/path/guidance without being literal. Evokes both the maze-solving and the artifact (thread) that makes it possible.
risk: Longer name (7 letters, 4 syllables), less familiar to non-classical audiences, potential pronunciation variance.

name: Skein
rationale: A coiled bundle of thread or yarn. Captures the idea of many parallel strands that must be unwound, worked, and rewound into a finished artifact.
why_creative: Concrete craft noun with both literal (thread bundle) and metaphorical (tangled work) readings. Short, CLI-friendly, visually distinctive.
risk: Obscure word outside craft/textile contexts; may need explanation on first encounter.

name: Loom
rationale: The frame that holds threads under tension while weaving. A system that structures independent pieces into a finished artifact through repeated passes.
why_creative: Four letters, one syllable, concrete tool metaphor. Evokes both the structure (frame) and the process (weaving passes = task loops).
risk: Can also mean 'to appear threateningly,' which conflicts with calm control positioning.

name: Wyrd
rationale: Old English/Norse concept of fate as a woven web. The Norns weave wyrd from past actions into present outcomes. Captures deterministic execution and verifiable results.
why_creative: Four letters, one syllable, archaic but memorable. Ties fate/determinism to weaving metaphor. Unusual spelling adds distinctiveness.
risk: Homophone with 'weird' creates pronunciation/spelling confusion and potential negative associations.

name: Moira
rationale: Greek word for fate, also the name of the Fates who spin, measure, and cut the thread of life. Represents the system that allocates, executes, and completes tasks.
why_creative: Five letters, two syllables, classical reference with thread/fate duality. Less common than Fates but more ownable.
risk: Also a common given name, which may reduce brand distinctiveness.

name: Spindle
rationale: The tool that twists fiber into thread. Represents the transformation of raw inputs (prompts, tasks) into structured, usable outputs (verified artifacts).
why_creative: Concrete craft tool with transformation metaphor. Seven letters but clear pronunciation and familiar shape.
risk: Slightly longer; 'spin' can imply rotation/confusion rather than convergence.

name: Strand
rationale: A single thread or fiber, or the act of weaving them together. Captures both the independent tasks and their assembly into a coherent whole.
why_creative: Six letters, one syllable, dual meaning (noun: thread; verb: weave/beach). Clean, CLI-friendly, familiar word with technical depth.
risk: 'Stranded' has negative connotations of being stuck or abandoned.

name: Chiron
rationale: The wise centaur who trained heroes. Represents a system that guides and teaches agents to execute correctly, looping until they pass their trials (checks).
why_creative: Six letters, two syllables, mentor/teacher archetype. Less common than other Greek names, more ownable.
risk: Pronunciation ambiguity (KY-ron vs SHEER-on); centaur imagery may feel whimsical rather than serious.

name: Sibyl
rationale: Ancient prophetesses who delivered oracles. Represents a system that provides authoritative, verifiable answers through structured interrogation (checks).
why_creative: Five letters, two syllables, oracle/truth archetype. Implies authoritative verification without AI clichés.
risk: Also a given name; oracle metaphor may imply prediction rather than verification.

name: Hestia
rationale: Greek goddess of the hearth, home, and domestic order. Represents the calm, reliable center that coordinates household (system) activities.
why_creative: Six letters, three syllables, calm/order archetype. Less warlike than Athena, more grounded than abstract fate figures.
risk: Longer, less familiar, domestic metaphor may feel too soft for technical infrastructure.

name: Thane
rationale: Scottish/Norse title for a lord's retainer who executes tasks with authority. Represents agents that carry out delegated work with accountability.
why_creative: Five letters, one syllable, duty/execution metaphor. Shakespearean (Macbeth) and historical resonance without being overused.
risk: Feudal hierarchy metaphor may not resonate with collaborative developer culture.

name: Rune
rationale: Ancient symbols with both literal meaning and magical significance. Represents tasks/checks as inscribed rules that must be satisfied for the spell (build) to work.
why_creative: Four letters, one syllable, symbol/rule duality. Evokes both writing (code) and verification (magic must work).
risk: Gaming/fantasy associations may reduce technical credibility; 'rune' can feel mystical rather than deterministic.

name: Aegis
rationale: The protective shield of Zeus/Athena, also meaning sponsorship or protection. Represents a system that guards execution quality through checks and verification.
why_creative: Five letters, two syllables, protection/authority metaphor. Implies both defense (checks) and sponsorship (orchestration).
risk: Pronunciation ambiguity (EE-jis vs AY-jis); protection metaphor may emphasize defense over execution.

name: Stratum
rationale: Geological layers that build upon each other, each verifiable and stable before the next forms. Captures the layered, foundational nature of task execution where each layer must pass checks.
why_creative: Strong, grounded metaphor for layered execution. Uncommon in dev tools but immediately understandable.
risk: Two valid pronunciations could cause confusion

name: Apex
rationale: The convergence point where all paths meet — the top of the DAG where all tasks complete and the final result emerges. Implies reaching the optimal solution.
why_creative: Short, punchy, implies peak performance and goal achievement. Works well as a CLI command.
risk: Used by Salesforce (Apex programming language), may have trademark conflicts

name: Vertex
rationale: A node in a graph where edges meet — the fundamental unit of a DAG. Each task is a vertex, each dependency an edge. Pure graph theory.
why_creative: Technically precise for DAG-based systems, sounds sharp and modern. Strong CLI feel.
risk: May feel too technical or academic for broader developer audience

name: Prism
rationale: Takes one input (a complex problem) and splits it into component parts (spectrum of tasks), then recombines them into a complete solution. Diverge-converge made visual.
why_creative: Beautiful metaphor for decomposition and recomposition. Memorable, ownable, premium feel.
risk: Prisma ORM is a major dev tool — too close for comfort

name: Kernel
rationale: The core computational unit that executes operations — in Converge's case, the runtime that orchestrates agents and verifies results. Essential, foundational, irreducible.
why_creative: Deeply technical credibility, implies low-level power and control. Familiar to developers.
risk: Heavily overloaded term (OS kernels, Jupyter kernels, ML kernels) — may lack distinctiveness

name: Catalyst
rationale: Enables reactions (task execution) without being consumed — the orchestration layer that makes agent work happen efficiently and repeatably.
why_creative: Implies acceleration and enablement. Strong metaphor for what orchestration does.
risk: Three syllables, slightly longer. Generic enough that trademark/domain may be contested

name: Helix
rationale: Spiral structure that iterates upward — like Converge's retry loops that spiral toward convergence, each attempt building on the last until checks pass.
why_creative: Elegant shape, implies progress through iteration. Distinctive and memorable.
risk: Perforce Helix is a version control system — potential confusion in dev tool space

name: Orbit
rationale: Stable, repeatable paths — like playbooks that run the same way every time. Tasks orbit around the goal until they lock into stable completion.
why_creative: Implies stability, predictability, and cyclical refinement. Clean, simple, ownable.
risk: May feel too abstract or disconnected from the concrete work of task execution

name: Pulse
rationale: Rhythmic execution — agents firing, tasks completing, checks running. The heartbeat of automated workflow.
why_creative: One syllable, energetic, implies life and continuous operation. Great CLI feel.
risk: Generic enough that many products use it — may be hard to own

name: Substrate
rationale: The underlying layer on which reactions occur — the runtime foundation that agents execute upon. Technical precision for the orchestration layer.
why_creative: Uncommon in dev tools, technically credible, implies foundational infrastructure.
risk: Three syllables, may feel academic. Polkadot's Substrate framework exists in blockchain space

name: Vortex
rationale: Converging flow — all tasks spiral inward toward the final result. Dynamic, powerful, implies inevitable convergence.
why_creative: Strong visual metaphor, energetic, implies powerful convergence. Memorable and distinctive.
risk: May feel chaotic rather than controlled — doesn't emphasize verification/reliability

name: Axis
